title: Gold Star Mother's and Family's Day, 2025
summary:
The President issued a proclamation marking Sunday, September 28, 2025, as Gold Star Mother’s and Family’s Day, honoring the families of service members who died in the line of duty and calling on Americans to display the flag and hold ceremonies in their memory.

This message is meant to uplift Gold Star families by recognizing their loss, resilience, and the lasting weight of their sacrifice. It underscores a commitment to support them, including a pledge from the Commander in Chief to stand by military families and pursue “peace through strength” so fewer families face such grief. It also reminds the public and government officials to show visible respect, and notes that this day has been recognized by Congress since 1936, reinforcing its place in national tradition.

Some may feel uneasy that the proclamation references the 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal and faults the previous administration’s response to affected families. For those who prefer that commemorations remain strictly nonpolitical, this could be seen as introducing partisan tones into a day of remembrance. Others who disagree with the policy framing may also take issue.

At its core, the proclamation asks the country to pause, remember, and show gratitude to families who have carried the cost of war. It invites a shared moment of recognition for their loved ones’ service and a renewed commitment to supporting them, now and in the future.
